blocks.costs: requests per second may fall: your floor is 2.52 (10% below this run's 2.8); TTFT worsens (requests wait longer to be admitted); throughput falls as fewer sequences run in each step
blocks.name: lower-concurrency
plan: then: a saturated GPU likely still binds
blocks.reason: the GPU was saturated with 96 sequences running at once, at the cap; half as many make each step shorter, so each token comes sooner

blocks.costs: the weights are quantized at every start; below compute capability 8.9 (T4, A10G) only the stored weights shrink, so prompt processing is no faster
blocks.name: fp8-weights
blocks.reason: highest sampled KV-cache usage 92%; vLLM can store the weights in 8-bit fp8 when it starts, so each decode step reads half the weight bytes and the freed memory holds more requests (on this GPU the maths runs in 8 bits too)
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 417 s to load, a 60 s window planned)

blocks.costs: a different checkpoint, which Tensward does not download: register it with `tensward init --project <new> --model <its directory>` (same --config and --prompts), then `tensward analyse --project <new> --baseline-answers <this run>/responses.jsonl` shows its answers next to this run's
blocks.name: quantized-checkpoint
blocks.reason: highest sampled KV-cache usage 92%; a pre-quantized copy of this model runs on this GPU (compute capability 8.9). 8-bit: int8 W8A8, fp8 (W8A8). 4-bit, where answers change more often: AWQ int4, GPTQ int4, W4A16. int8 W8A8 and fp8 also run prompt processing in 8-bit arithmetic here

blocks.costs: TPOT rises when answers do not copy the prompt, and at high concurrency; a slower start
blocks.name: ngram-speculation
blocks.reason: prompts are long (median 495 words beyond what they share). N-gram speculation drafts tokens by copying spans of the prompt, so it only helps when answers quote or repeat their input; otherwise it costs a little - compare TPOT with and without it. Replaying prompt lookup on this run's answers, drafts would supply 0.5% of the output of the 5% of answers they help least (the slowest once speculating); measure it: the step overhead on this model is not known
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 417 s to load, a 60 s window planned)

blocks.costs: does not change TPOT (fewer preemptions, but more sequences in each step); helps throughput and TTFT; less memory headroom: the engine may fail to start
blocks.name: more-kv-memory
blocks.reason: highest sampled KV-cache usage 92%; kv_memory_fraction is the engine default. A larger share leaves the GPU less memory headroom, so the engine may fail to start or run out of memory
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 417 s to load, a 60 s window planned)

blocks.costs: does not change TPOT (less KV read per step, but more sequences in each step); helps throughput and TTFT; Qwen2 and Qwen2.5 models lose their answers with it; speed changed little in Tensward's runs on an L4 and an A10G
blocks.name: fp8-kv-cache
blocks.reason: highest sampled KV-cache usage 92%; a fp8 KV cache holds about twice the tokens
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 417 s to load, a 60 s window planned)

blocks.costs: does not change TPOT (fewer preemptions, but more sequences in each step); helps throughput and TTFT; requests with images are rejected
blocks.name: no-media-encoders
blocks.reason: the checkpoint takes images and video but no prompt sends any; serving only its text model stops the engine reserving memory for the media encoders and lifts the minimum batch size they impose (requests with images would then be rejected)
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 417 s to load, a 60 s window planned)

blocks.text: `trim-max-context-len`: vLLM gives the KV cache the memory left after loading the model whatever max_context_len is, and a request takes blocks only as it grows; trimming it adds no room and only refuses longer requests
